A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 41-page versions of AnyEdit. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–H support direct comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-quality measurements, editing experiments and ablations in Tables 3–6, human evaluations in Tables 10–12, and detailed benchmark results in Tables 15–17.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, human evaluations and appendix results.

M1.justification: Appendix G.4, Table 8 changes the reported expert organization from eleven experts to nine, removing the implicit/relation and local-editing expert entries and renumbering the remainder. The projector, routing mechanism, task embeddings, objectives and two-stage training remain. This establishes a limited revision to the stated configuration, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same source datasets, five editing categories, 25 editing types, and EMU-Edit, MagicBrush and AnyEdit-Test evaluations. Supplementary visual-reference and multi-turn scenarios are also retained. Count and label revisions do not establish changed coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables, human evaluations and supplementary qualitative comparisons. Table 1's revised characterization of SEED-Data-Edit does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Table 7 revises the reported dataset counts by six examples, and Table 8 specifies nine rather than eleven experts. These are limited reported sample-size and model-configuration revisions. Test selection, metrics, resolutions and training budgets remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Table 6 retains the routing, task-embedding and counterfactual-composition ablations, and Figure 4 retains the same data-scaling analysis. Supplementary robustness examples, multi-turn editing and other case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Seed settings in Table 9 and human-score averaging in Appendix H.1 are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 7 changes Action Change instruction/image counts from 47,216 to 47,210 and total instructions from 2,506,409 to 2,506,403. Benchmark scores, ablation results and human evaluations remain unchanged. The retained image total of 2,180,350 now disagrees with v3's image rows, which sum to 2,180,344.

T1.justification: The diffusion objectives, attention equations and classifier-free guidance derivations in Section 4 and Appendices G.1–G.3 are unchanged. Equation 2 is relocated, without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The core contributions and performance claims remain: AnyEdit, its adaptive collection pipeline, AnySD and AnyEdit-Test. Section 3.1 changes '2M' to '2.5M', aligning with the dataset size already claimed in v1's abstract, statistics and conclusion.

C2.justification: Interpretations of architectural benefits, data scaling, counterfactual generalization and benchmark limitations remain unchanged. Appendix discussions of automatic metrics versus human preferences and MagicBrush's collection bias are also retained.

D1.justification: Table 8 revises the expert-to-task specification. Section 4.2's shortened Stage I description no longer explicitly states that original images and instructions are randomly omitted during training. Hardware, hyperparameters, baseline configurations and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Table 1 now credits SEED-Data-Edit with camera-movement support and open-source availability, both marked absent in v1. The cited works and broader related-work discussion otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited edits streamline the abstract, routing explanation and Stage I description, correct terminology such as 'inpainting' to 'outpainting', update author credits and affiliation, and add acknowledgments. The main section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 corrects the segmentation example's label and camera-movement wording, while Figure 3 receives typography and spacing changes. Table 8 loses two expert rows, Equation 2 moves onto page 5, and text reflows. The experimental displays and appendix example collections are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the inconsistent '2M' description and corrects figure labels. However, Table 7 introduces an inconsistent image total, and Table 8 removes local and implicit expert assignments without explaining how those tasks are handled. The PDFs do not establish whether the expert revision corrects the architecture description or leaves necessary information missing. These benefits and documentation concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
